June 3 marks [World Bicycle Day](https://www.un.org/en/observances/bicycle-day), an official UN observance celebrated to draw attention to the benefits of using a bike, a healthy, affordable and environmentally friendly way of getting from A to B.

**On this day, people are encouraged to leave their cars behind and hop on their bikes for their daily commute to work.**

After all, cycling to work is still relatively rare in the United States, despite the many benefits it offers in terms of personal health, reduced traffic and emissions savings.

Number Of Zombie Properties Increase In 30 US States

The number of zombie homes - vacant properties abandoned by owners during the foreclosure process - rose in 30 U.S. states and the District of Columbia in the second quarter of this year from the previous quarter, real estate data analytics company ATTOM said in a May 29 statement.

Zombie homes, which can fall into disrepair and negatively impact the value of other properties in the neighborhood, are a sign of distress in the housing market and the broader economy.

Four young travelers once set out from their homes in different villages to find a new land. One came from the forest, one from the mountains, one from the fields, and one from the coast. Each had grown up learning only the ways of their own people.

The mountain traveler said, “Strength and silence are the highest ways.”
The forest traveler said, “Gentleness and patience are better.”
The field traveler said, “Work and order make the world right.”
The coastal traveler said, “Freedom and feeling bring life.”

They walked together, but soon began to argue. “You’re doing it wrong,” one would say. “Your way doesn’t make sense,” said another. They each tried to lead, and the road split apart.

At night, a wise elder met them by a fire. She gave them bread and said, “You come from one land, though you don’t remember. The path ahead cannot be walked alone.”

They looked at the fire. They looked at the bread. They looked at each other. Slowly, without a word, they returned to the same road. Each still carried their own way—but they began to listen, and to share.

When they finally reached the new land, it felt like home. Not because it matched any one of their ways, but because they had learned to walk it together.

The story shows that people grow up with different ideas about how to live. Each person thinks their way is best. But when they argue and separate, no one gets far.

Only when they walk together, share, listen, and learn from each other can they reach what they’re looking for. Unity doesn’t mean being the same. It means staying together and moving forward as one.

Start by living with quiet strength. Walk with others patiently, listen deeply, and let your actions show respect. People are more likely to receive a message when they feel seen, not corrected.

We each carry part of the path. Together, we find the way. Those who are ready will hear it, those who are not will remember. Truth shared gently becomes seed, while kindness and time water it.
